title: Is Robot trading GOLD profitable? MT5 Expert Advisor Study
author: tommytradez
selftext:
Ran a systematic sweep on XAUUSD to find out how much of a gold EA backtest is edge and how much is just not paying to trade. Posting it because the answer was more one-sided than expected.

**Setup**

* 2,050 generated strategies across M5, M15, M30, H1 and H4
* Each backtested on every full year from 2018 to 2025, so 16,400 strategy-years
* Every one of those run three times under different cost assumptions: modelled real spread, a flat 1 pip retail assumption, and zero cost
* 55,650 runs, 0 failures, starting equity 10,000 each time
* Median modelled spread on gold came out around 3.8 pips

**1. The strategies that survive all 8 years only exist when trading is free**

Number of strategies profitable in every single one of the 8 years:

* Real spread: **0**
* Flat 1 pip: **0**
* Zero cost: **12**

Same strategies, same data, same years. The only variable was whether they paid to trade.

**2. Costs flip a quarter of everything**

* 4,314 of 16,400 strategy-years (26.3%) are profitable with costs off and unprofitable with real spread charged
* With the flat 1 pip assumption it is 1,731 (10.6%)

**3. The base rate is grim**

Real spread arm, across all 16,400 strategy-years:

* median annual return **-17.5%**
* only **19.1%** of strategy-years finished positive
* median max drawdown -28.9%
* best single year +173%, worst -100%

That +173% is the number that would get screenshotted. It sits in a pool where four out of five lose money.

**4. The timeframe gradient is just a spread bill**

Median annual return, share of profitable years, and median trades per year, all on real spread:

* M5: **-99.3%**, 0.0% positive, 966 trades
* M15: -56.3%, 5.2% positive, 497 trades
* M30: -32.1%, 8.2% positive, 292 trades
* H1: -12.7%, 21.1% positive, 160 trades
* H4: **-1.6%**, 39.5% positive, 39 trades

Spread per trade barely moves across those rows, between 3.7 and 4.0 pips. The only thing that changes is how many times you pay it. On M5, out of 1,200 strategy-years, not one finished green.

**Takeaway**

When a gold EA shows a smooth multi-year curve, the first thing to check is not the entry logic, it is what spread the test charged. On this data, the entire difference between "profitable every year for 8 years" and "does not exist" was that one setting.

These are backtest returns, not achievable ones, and gold is a wide-spread instrument so it punishes frequency harder than most. Nothing here is financial advice.
